elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of oral probiotic supplementation for acne vulgaris
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review (and meta-analysis).

elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of oral probiotic supplementation for acne vulgaris using contemporary randomeffects methods.
elements.reason: The Background and Objectives section states the main objective clearly.

elements.quote: Eligible studies were double-blind randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing oral probiotics with placebo or standard therapy for ≥ 4 weeks and reporting quantitative acne severity outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies main inclusion criteria for eligible studies.

elements.quote: we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov through November 2025 without language restrictions
elements.reason: Information sources are named and the last search date (November 2025) is reported.

elements.quote: Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2.0.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk-of-bias assessment method.

elements.quote: Standardized mean differences (SMDs) were pooled using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was summarized using I 2 , τ 2 (95% CI), and 95% prediction intervals.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the synthesis methods used to present and combine results.

elements.quote: Three RCTs ( n = 231) met eligibility criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and participants; study characteristics (double-blind RCTs of oral probiotics) are summarized.

elements.quote: Pooled analysis suggested a modest reduction in inflammatory lesion counts favoring probiotics (SMD - 0.57; 95% CI - 0.94 to - 0.21)
elements.reason: Results for the main outcome (inflammatory lesion counts) are reported with effect estimate; adverse events and risk of bias results are also summarized.
A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports the summary estimate with its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: a modest reduction in inflammatory lesion counts favoring probiotics
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and that probiotics were favored.

elements.quote: the current evidence base is small and heterogeneous, and the certainty of effect remains low-to-moderate
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes key limitations including small evidence base, heterogeneity, and low-to-moderate certainty.

elements.quote: Oral probiotics may modestly reduce acne severity as a generally safe, antibiotic-sparing adjunct; however... Larger, standardized RCTs are required before firm clinical recommendations can be made.
elements.reason: The Conclusions section provides interpretation of results and their implications.

elements.quote: Funding: This research received no external funding.
elements.reason: The abstract includes a funding statement specifying the source of funding (none).

elements.quote: Registration: PROSPERO CRD420251181388.
elements.reason: The abstract provides both the register name (PROSPERO) and registration number.

elements.reason: The PRISMA checklist claims item 3 is completed in the Introduction, but no actual Introduction text describing the current state of knowledge or uncertainties was retrieved. Only the checklist assertion is available, not the underlying content.
No retrieved evidence contains text from the Introduction explaining the importance of or need for this review; only the checklist table asserts compliance without the actual rationale content.

No retrieved evidence indicates whether similar systematic reviews exist or whether the need for an updated/current review relative to prior reviews is discussed. The Introduction rationale content was not retrieved.

This is a review of an intervention (oral probiotics for acne), so a description of the proposed mechanism of action is relevant, but no retrieved evidence shows the Introduction describing probiotic mechanisms of action in acne.

Oral probiotics administered as a single intervention in RCTs is not a complex intervention with multiple interacting components requiring a logic model; the retrieved evidence does not indicate a complex delivery context.

elements.quote: The primary objectives of this study were to (i) estimate the pooled effect of oral probiotic supplementation on clinically assessed acne severity, (ii) quantify between-study heterogeneity and explore potential sources of variability, and (iii) appraise the overall certainty and real-world applicability of the current evidence base.
elements.reason: The Introduction explicitly enumerates the review's objectives in a structured, question-formulation-like manner (pooled effect, heterogeneity, certainty of evidence).

elements.quote: we conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis focusing exclusively on double-blind randomized controlled trials of oral probiotics for acne vulgaris
elements.reason: Population (adults with acne vulgaris), intervention (oral probiotics), and study design (double-blind RCTs) are indicated, but no explicit PICO-formatted statement of planned comparisons (e.g., probiotics vs placebo) is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Studies were selected according to pre-specified inclusion and exclusion criteria structured around the PICOS framework: Population: Humans diagnosed with acne vulgaris (any severity), confirmed by clinical criteria. Intervention: Oral probiotics, any strain(s), formulation, or dose. Comparator: Placebo or standard acne therapy (e.g., topical treatments). Outcomes: Quantitative acne severity outcomes... Study Design: Double-blind randomized controlled trials (RCTs) lasting ≥ 4 weeks.
elements.reason: Full PICOS-based eligibility criteria are specified, including population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, and study design with minimum duration.

No dissemination year limits, language restrictions, or publication status criteria are reported; only study-type exclusions (e.g., non-peer-reviewed abstracts) are mentioned, without year or language specifications.

elements.quote: Exclusion criteria: ... lack of extractable numeric outcomes
elements.reason: The review mentions exclusion for 'lack of extractable numeric outcomes' but does not distinguish between studies where outcomes were not measured versus outcomes measured but results not reported.
No evidence describes how studies were grouped for the syntheses or links groups to the review's defined comparisons; only that three trials entered qualitative and quantitative synthesis (text_21).

elements.quote: Exclusion criteria: Non-randomized studies, open-label or single-blind trials, topical probiotics, synbiotic/prebiotic-only studies, animal or in vitro studies, lack of extractable numeric outcomes, and non-non-peerreviewed abstracts.
elements.reason: Notable restrictions (e.g., double-blind design only, ≥4 weeks duration, exclusion of synbiotic/prebiotic-only studies) are stated without any rationale.

elements.quote: Date of final search: 4 November 2025

elements.reason: Number of reviewers (two) and independence are reported, but disagreement-resolution procedures are not described.
No evidence that authors sought or confirmed risk-of-bias information from study investigators; no such process is reported, so this conditional element does not apply.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are mentioned; assessment was performed manually by two reviewers.

elements.quote: For continuous outcomes, standardized mean differences (SMD) using Hedges g were calculated. Corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI) were extracted or derived from reported summary statistics.
elements.reason: The Effect Measures section explicitly specifies SMD (Hedges g) with 95% CI for the continuous outcomes synthesized; results sections confirm SMD was used for the primary outcome.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect size magnitude (e.g., small/medium/large SMD cutoffs) or their rationale are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: When not directly provided, means and standard deviations were reconstructed from medians, ranges, or interquartile ranges using validated methods (standard meta-analytic conversions; see Cochrane Handbook) [36].
elements.reason: The manuscript describes conversion of summary statistics (medians/ranges/IQRs to means/SDs) to enable SMD computation, which is a form of re-expression, but no re-expression of synthesized results into another effect measure (e.g., SMD to odds ratio) is described.
The choice of SMD/Hedges g is stated but no explicit justification (e.g., differing measurement scales across trials) is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: These reports were assessed for eligibility according to the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria... Ultimately, three double-blind randomized controlled trials (n = 231 participants) met all inclusion criteria and were included in the qualitative and quantitative synthesis.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the eligibility assessment process (predefined PICOS criteria in text_12, full-text assessment and exclusion reasons in text_21, PRISMA flow diagram in Figure 1), and states included studies entered both qualitative and quantitative synthesis. However, it does not explicitly describe processes for deciding study eligibility for each separate synthesis (e.g., tabulating intervention characteristics against planned synthesis groups), likely because only three trials fed a single synthesis. The decision process is therefore only partially described.

elements.quote: When not directly provided, means and standard deviations were reconstructed from medians, ranges, or interquartile ranges using validated methods (standard meta-analytic conversions; see Cochrane Handbook) [36].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes data preparation methods: reconstruction of missing means/SDs from medians/ranges/IQRs using validated Cochrane Handbook conversions, and derivation of 95% CIs from reported summary statistics. This is corroborated by text_44 noting conversion of medians to means for one study.

No methods text describes the tabular structures used to display results of individual studies or syntheses. Tables are only referenced indirectly via the PRISMA checklist (e.g., 'Results 3.2 + Table 3'), without any description in the Methods of what data the tables contain or how they were constructed.

elements.quote: Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plot visualization and Egger's regression test ( p < 0.05 suggestive) [40].
elements.reason: The Methods describe the funnel plot as a graphical display for publication bias, but do not describe other graphical displays of results (e.g., forest plots for the meta-analysis, referenced only indirectly as 'Figure 2' in the checklist), so the description of graphical methods is incomplete.

No evidence reports the basis for ordering or grouping studies within tables or graphs. The only related mention is cumulative meta-analysis 'by publication year' (text_18), but no ordering/grouping basis for tables or plots of individual studies is stated.
No non-standard graphs are reported; only conventional displays (funnel plot, flow diagram, figures) are used, so no rationale for non-standard graphs is required.

elements.quote: All analyses were conducted using R (metafor package).
elements.reason: Software (R) and package (metafor) are reported, but no version numbers are given.
Meta-analysis was performed, so an alternative non-meta-analytic synthesis method does not apply.

elements.quote: The primary quantitative synthesis used a random-effects model based on Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) with Hartung-Knapp (HK) adjustment for more accurate variance estimation under small sample sizes
elements.reason: The model (random-effects REML with HK adjustment) and its rationale (small sample sizes) are reported.

elements.quote: Secondary sensitivity analyses included: DerSimonian-Laird (DL) random-effects estimator; Leave-one-out (LOO) influence analysis; Alternative variance estimators (Paule-Mandel); Cumulative meta-analysis by publication year
elements.reason: Statistical methods for the meta-analysis, including primary and sensitivity estimators, are described.

elements.quote: Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using: I 2 (percentage of variation due to heterogeneity); τ 2 (between-study variance, with 95% CI using Q-profile); Cochran's Q test; 95% Prediction Interval (PI)
elements.reason: Methods to identify and quantify heterogeneity (I², τ², Cochran's Q, prediction intervals) are reported.

elements.quote: a random-effects model based on Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML)
elements.reason: The between-study variance estimator (REML, with Paule-Mandel and DL as sensitivity alternatives) is reported.

elements.quote: with Hartung-Knapp (HK) adjustment for more accurate variance estimation
elements.reason: The Hartung-Knapp adjustment, which determines confidence interval calculation for the summary effect, is reported.

elements.quote: τ 2 (between-study variance, with 95% CI using Q-profile)
elements.reason: Additional implementation details such as Q-profile CIs for τ² and prediction intervals are reported.
A frequentist (REML/DL) meta-analysis was performed; no Bayesian meta-analysis was conducted, so priors do not apply.
No methods for handling statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: meta-regression and formal subgroup analyses could not be conducted because only three trials met the inclusion criteria
elements.reason: Planned syntheses (meta-regression, subgroup analyses) judged impossible are identified with reasons.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses were conducted to explore whether differences in clinical or methodological characteristics could plausibly account for the observed heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes subgroup analyses as the method used to explore causes of heterogeneity, alongside heterogeneity statistics (I2, tau2, Q, prediction interval) in text_18.

elements.quote: Treatment duration (<8 weeks vs. ≥ 8 weeks) was evaluated as a potential modifier... Baseline acne severity was examined... dosage- and concentration-based comparisons were explored to assess whether higher-strength or multi-strain probiotic formulations exerted systematically different effects.
elements.reason: Factors (severity, duration, dosage) and levels for duration are reported with rationale, but levels for severity and dosage are not fully specified and no expected direction of effect modification is explicitly stated.
No evidence reports whether subgroup analyses used study-level variables, within-study contrasts, or both.

elements.quote: Given the limited number of trials, subgroup analyses are descriptive and hypothesisgenerating only.
elements.reason: The manuscript states subgroup analyses were descriptive only, but no specific method for comparing subgroup effects (e.g., interaction tests) is reported.

elements.quote: meta-regression and formal subgroup analyses could not be conducted because only three trials met the inclusion criteria
elements.reason: Meta-analysis was performed (three trials quantitatively synthesized), so the conditional requirement for informal heterogeneity exploration when meta-analysis is unsuitable does not apply.

elements.quote: Although these subgroup analyses were exploratory and constrained by the small number of available trials...
elements.reason: Subgroup analyses are labeled exploratory, but the manuscript does not explicitly state whether they were pre-specified or not.

elements.quote: Several sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness of the pooled effect. Leave-one-out analysis demonstrated that removal of any single study produced only modest fluctuations in the magnitude of the pooled SMD... analyses excluding studies with higher risk-of-bias ratings yielded effect estimates consistent with the primary analysis... Re-synthesizing the data using alternative estimators-including fixed-effect, DerSimonianLaird, and Hartung-Knapp-adjusted random-effects models-produced convergent results... Restricting the analysis to trials employing more standardized outcome assessment scales did not materially change the pooled estimate.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes multiple sensitivity analyses (leave-one-out, exclusion by risk of bias, alternative estimators, restriction to standardized outcome scales) and their results, fully covering the reporting of sensitivity analyses conducted.
No evidence indicates which sensitivity analyses were pre-specified versus conducted post hoc; the methods (text_18) list secondary analyses but do not identify any as not pre-specified.

elements.quote: Risk of publication bias and small-study effects was evaluated using funnel plots, regression-based asymmetry testing (Egger's test), and comparison of REML-HK vs. DL estimators [40,41].
elements.reason: Methods for assessing reporting/publication bias are explicitly specified in the Methods section.

elements.quote: Risk of publication bias and small-study effects was evaluated using funnel plots, regression-based asymmetry testing (Egger's test), and comparison of REML-HK vs. DL estimators [40,41].
elements.reason: No existing domain-based reporting-bias tool with assessed domains or a process for deriving an overall judgement is described; only funnel plots and Egger's test are used, without a structured overall judgement procedure.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are reported, and none appear to have been made.
